messages:
Maya Patel: heads up — we just got a spike of p99 errors/latency reports from a handful of customers after last night's runtime rollout in eu-west. Support escalated, users seeing 3-6x p99 for text-generation. filing here so eng-runtime can triage :warning:

Toni Chen: Yikes. Which rollout ID/version? Can you paste the deployment tag and any customer IDs? :eyes:

Maya Patel: rollout: runtime-v1.13.0 (canary -> rolling). Affected region: eu-west-1. SupportBot attached customer repro for 3 accounts (redspark, voyager-inc, studyapp).

SupportBot: attached repro steps:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-open-7b", "input":"Summarize: <long document with ~1200 tokens>", "max_tokens":512, "stream":false}'
2) observed latency: 1.2s p50, 4.3s p95, 12.8s p99 (normally p99 < 2s)
3) traces show CPU-bound stalls on GPU host during key exchange/kv cache warmup

Adrián Rivera: I can start the bisect on canaries. Quick checks: did we change kernel selector heuristics or batching defaults in v1.13?

Kai Nguyen: yes — v1.13 changed kernel selector to prefer fused-attn for seq_len > 512 and bumped default max_batch_size from 16 -> 24 for dense models to improve throughput. Also added an experimental commit that defers kv-cache hydration for first token to reduce tail latencies on short requests.

Toni Chen: hm deferred kv-cache hydration sounds suspicious for long inputs — that could cause extra work on first few tokens and stall tail. But p99 for long inputs? maybe kernel selector chose a slower kernel path for particular GPU driver combo.

Maya Patel: Support logs show spikes correlated to requests with long prompt prefix (~1200 tokens) that then generate ~512 tokens. So heavy KV usage.

Adrián Rivera: I'm going to query metrics. Running PromQL for last 30m: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{region=\"eu-west-1\",job=\"runtime-service\"}[5m])) by (le))

Adrián Rivera: result: p99 jumped from ~1.8s to 11.2s across canaries in last deploy window. p95 up to ~4.7s. Error rate normal, so not retries, latency-only.

Kai Nguyen: pulling canary host logs now. tail -n 200 /var/log/runtime/containers/runtime-service.log | grep \"kernel_selector\" -A4 -B2

[log excerpt]
kernel_selector: selected fused-attn-v2 for model redwood-open-7b, seq_len=1536, batch=18
kv_cache: hydration deferred for request id=req-84a3..
mem_manager: peak GPU mem 98%, attempted allocation fallback to CPU
latency_tracker: token_latency_ms=5432 for token 3 of request req-84a3

Kai Nguyen: that mem_manager line worries me — fused-attn path uses more temp memory on our older A100 kernels and with larger batches we're hitting memory pressure and falling back to slower paths or CPU copies. That would blow up p99.

Toni Chen: canary config shows autoscaler didn't kick because we didn't label these canaries for burst. Might be two compounding changes: larger batch + fused-attn selection + deferred kv hydrating causing first-token stall while memory copies happen.

Maya Patel: customers want a mitigation asap. Suggestions?

Adrián Rivera: immediate mitigation options (ranked):
- rollback runtime-v1.13.0 to v1.12.3 for eu-west canaries (fastest to revert global behavior).
- hotfix: force kernel_selector to fallback to legacy-attn for sequences > 1024 on A100 driver versions < 1.2.0 (requires config patch, less disruptive).
- reduce default max_batch_size back to 16 for rolling nodes (config override) and disable deferred-kv hydration feature flag.

Kai Nguyen: I can flip the feature flag for deferred_kv_hydration off on canary group in ~5 minutes. That is low-risk and quick. Also can push a runtime config override to reduce batch size.

Toni Chen: Rolling flags would let us measure effect before rollback. Do it for canaries and watch p99. If no improvement we rollback.

Maya Patel: please coordinate with support — I'll tell affected customers we're working on a mitigation and will update in 30m.

DeployBot: starting config update on runtime-canary-eu-west: set deferred_kv_hydration=false, runtime.max_batch_size=16 (change-id: cfg-20260315-01)

Adrián Rivera: after flag flip, PromQL over 5m windows shows p99 back down to ~2.1s on canaries within 12 minutes. p95 back to ~1.9s. From: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{region=\"eu-west-1\",canary=\"true\"}[5m])) by (le))

Kai Nguyen: logs after change: kernel_selector still picks fused-attn, but token_latency_ms for first tokens drops dramatically because kv cache hydration now synchronous and completes earlier, less head-of-line blocking. Memory pressure still present on some nodes but not causing CPU fallback as often because batch sizes smaller.

Maya Patel: great — customers reporting improved response times. Should we proceed to roll back v1.13 globally or do a targeted hotfix?

Toni Chen: plan: 1) pause further rollout of v1.13 globally (pause done). 2) revert default max_batch_size in runtime config to 16 cluster-wide as short term. 3) create hotfix for kernel_selector heuristics to avoid fused-attn on older drivers/packets and ensure safe memory footprints. 4) run a trimmed canary with hotfix and full telemetry (p50/p95/p99 + mem/copy rates) for 2 hours before resuming.

Adrián Rivera: I'll open a PR for kernel selector changes and add a test fixture that simulates seq_len 1500 + batch 18 on driver matrix. Also add an e2e perf test to our canary pipeline.

Kai Nguyen: note for SRE: add an alert that triggers when p99 / baseline_p99 > 2x AND memory_copy_fallback_count > 0 for the job; currently we only alert on errors not copies.

Maya Patel: thanks team. I'll compile notes for the customer update and incident summary. Can we add a short repro and suggested mitigation in the support KB (how to avoid hitting this: split prompts <1024, or temporarily set max_tokens lower)?

Toni Chen: yes — add support KB and include curl reproduction + recommended workaround: set max_batching_tokens or connection level hints, and mention we have a fix in progress.

Maya Patel: follow-ups: Adrián to PR kernel-selector hotfix (ETA 6h), Kai to extend alerts and mem metrics (ETA 3h), Toni to update KB and pause rollout (done), Maya to prepare customer comms (30m). We'll reconvene in 2 hours. :thumbsup:
